Name: CAL_ign_target_step_advance_accel_pedal_manual
EOL Comment: ign_target_step_advance — how fast timing comes back. This table sets the rate limit on ignition timing moving in the advance direction: when the ECU's timing target rises above what's currently being run\, this is the biggest bite it's allowed to take\, and it takes one bite every 50 ms. Values are quarter-degrees\, so degrees per second = value × 5 — a stock value of 8 means the ECU will only feed timing back in at 40 °/s. It's looked up on RPM × accelerator pedal\, and stock is a flat 8 (40 °/s) across most of the map\, rising to 12–40 (60–200 °/s) only at high RPM with the pedal down. Raise it and timing is restored faster\, giving a sharper reconnect out of a cut\, but push it too far and the torque returns as a bump instead of a build. Lower it and recovery is smoother\, but the engine sits retarded longer than it needs to and feels soft and lazy after shifts or interventions. The high-RPM\, high-pedal cells are the ones worth raising for a crisper reconnect; leave the light-pedal cells slow.

Name: CAL_ign_target_step_retard_accel_pedal
EOL Comment: ign_target_step_retard — how fast timing gets pulled. Same rate limit in the opposite direction: when the timing target drops\, this is the largest amount of timing the ECU may remove per step\, again one step every 50 ms\, again in quarter-degrees\, so degrees per second = value × 5. It's on the same RPM × pedal axes and it's by far the more pedal-sensitive of the two. Stock is just 2–4 (10–20 °/s) at light pedal\, climbing through 8\, 16 and 32 to 40 (200 °/s) as the pedal opens\, and the whole 4000 RPM column is set to 255 — a step large enough that the rate limit is effectively switched off above that speed. The slow light-pedal numbers are deliberate: pulling timing quickly at cruise makes a hole you can feel for no benefit. The fast high-pedal numbers exist because a target drop under load usually means something that needs to act immediately. Raising the light-pedal cells buys quicker response at the cost of drivability; lowering the high-pedal cells slows down the very interventions you want fast\, so be conservative there.

Name: CAL_dpm_torque_cut_p_term
EOL Comment: dpm_torque_cut_factor is the proportional part of the GT430's ECU traction control. Once the filtered slip error (how far wheel slip is above the target) passes CAL_dpm_intervention_threshold\, the ECU looks it up in the 6×10 table CAL_dpm_torque_cut_factor. That table is indexed by front-axle speed\, which is effectively vehicle speed since the fronts aren't driven\, and by slip error in 1/8 % steps. The ECU adds it to the integral term dpm_torque_cut_accumulated\, capping the sum to form dpm_torque_cut_total. That total sets how much of dpm_torque_when_tc_activated (the combustion torque captured when TC first stepped in) is removed. The result is torque_limit_dpm_spark\, floored at CAL_dpm_torque_min_allowed\, and the throttle limit is set a margin above it.
